simple.meaning: חֵלְכָא (chêlᵉkâʼ) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a wretch , i.e. unfortunate.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Psalms 10:8. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֵלְכָא (H2489) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H2489. chelekah ֵחלְכָה read חֶלְכֶּה חַלְכֶּה, , or חָלְכֶּה , adjective helpless, unfortunate , only as substantive hapless, luckless one(s) — לְֵחלְכָה Psa 10:8 , ᵐ5 εἰς τὸν πένητα , ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ; חֵלֶ֑כָה 10:14 ᵐ5 ὁ πτωχός ; חלכאים 10:10 Kt, read plural חַלְכָּאִים ( ׳חָל ׳חֶל, ); Qr ᵐ5 כָּאִים חֵל τῶν πενήτων . In all text and meaning dubious ( ᵑ0 reads חֵלְכָה = חֵילְךָ thine army ; and כָּאִים חֵל 10:10 army of dejected ones , but this against usage of חֵל , and no such figurative sense of חַיִל , see O1 Hup De Bae Che, and critical note) [ כָּאֶה ] adjective cowed , Psa 10:10 Qr כָּאִים חֵל ; host of cowed ones , but read Kt חלכאים .
definitions.rootNote: or חֵלְכָה ; apparently from an unused root probably meaning to be dark or (figuratively) unhappy;
